page.layout: One page of text in a single column with a running head and page number at the top. No margin notes. The rubric at the top is centred italic. Below it, a list of verb entries, one per line, followed by two indented paragraphs and a catchword at the lower right.

head.i: Recita verba, sicut Audio conjuganda, quæper-fecta & supina variant.

main_text.l: Aperio, ich thu auff/ich öffne/aperui, apertum.
Concio, ich bewege/ richte an / ich berüffe zusam-men / concivi, concitum, penultima longa: Conci-
tum, penultima brevi, est à verbo Concieo.
Confentio, ich bewillige/ ich hält es mit einem/ confensi, confensum.
Farcio, ich erfülle/ ich meste[?]/farsi, fartum.
Operio, ich bedecke/ ich beschliesse/operui, opertū.
Reperio, ich finde ohn geferd / ich erlange / ich er-dencke/reperi, repertum.
Sancio, ich ordene/ ich gebe ein gesetz/sancivi & san-xi, sancitum & sanctum.
Sarcio, ich flicke zusamen/ ich erstatte/sarsi[?], sartū.
Sentio, ich empfinde/ mercke/ hatte[?]/sensi[?], sensum.
main_text.p: In primo imperfecto verbi, Eo, dicimus ibam non iebam in primo futuro Eam & ibo in Gerudio, Eundi, eundum, eundo cum Compositis.
Hactenus de integris Verbis primæ formæ: sequu-tur Defectiva, quæ persona vel tempore deficiunt.

page.notes: Dark stain over the lines "Sarcio" and "Sentio" hides part of the words "sarfi" and "fenfi"; these readings are doubtful. "meste", "verzeuue" and "hatte" are German glosses in black letter that I could not read with certainty. "iebam" at the start of the second line of the paragraph is printed as shown, possibly a misprint. "Gerudio" is printed as shown (for Gerundio).
